entry.title: Directing the Night Shift: a Pi that plays, a Pocket Player, and site 3.2.0
entry.summary: Game-Maker: Sandbox Edition reached site version 3.2.0. In this post I describe a day where AI agents wrote most of the code while I directed: a Raspberry Pi that runs Game-Maker games, an improved Pocket Player, and other features. The full write-up is on my blog.

entry.title: THE CHEZ: running the engine from npm in a separate project
entry.summary: THE CHEZ is a small Vite and TypeScript app that tests whether the Game-Maker Sandbox engine can be installed from npm and run in a project of its own. Its bundled sample game, The Stripe Hypothesis, is there to prove the integration: Doc Leo swears racing stripes make THE CHEZ faster, Teddy has doubts, and the speedometer gets the last word. Version 0.2.0 now takes the engine, archive, and tools packages from npm. The game downloads as one ZIP and is unpacked by the archives package.

entry.title: Game-Maker OS wakes up on a Pi Zero
entry.summary: A bare-metal kernel for Game-Maker runs on a Raspberry Pi Zero W, shows its status on an e-ink display, and updates itself over one USB cable. The details and the story of getting there are on my blog.

entry.title: Pocket Players, pixel diplomas, and a growing Game-Maker Sandbox
entry.summary: Within two days, RSD Game-Maker gained a handheld player, 94 playable lessons, graduation features, and a level generator. Read how it came together on my blog.

entry.title: Tic-tac-toe and Crystal Palace 9
entry.summary: I trained a small tic-tac-toe model, Palace-9, ran into visualization, training, and tokenizer problems along the way, and planned a smaller follow-up called Crystal-9. Crystal-9 later became the model behind Crystal Palace 9 on the Commodore 64. The full story is on my blog.
